criteria.name: cw_custom_document_surface
criteria.description: Enter a distinctive word into the code editor by typing it or by pasting it with the usual shortcut, then inspect the live DOM read-only to find where that word is displayed. If neither puts the word into the editor, inspect where the source already shown in the editor is displayed instead. Fails if the displayed source text lives in a textarea, an input or an element with contenteditable enabled, including a transparent one layered over a highlighted copy, or if the editing area or its ancestors carry the root markers of a ready-made editor: class names cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap or ql-editor, the attribute data-slate-editor, or a DraftEditor class. Passes when the source is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, canvas or SVG. A small input or textarea that is used only to receive keyboard or clipboard events is allowed as long as it is not what shows the source to the user: the source the user sees must be drawn by the other elements. Judge only these observable DOM facts; do not judge how well the editor works here.
criteria.reasoning: Typed the distinctive word ZEBRAFROSTWORD into the editor with real key presses (click into #editorWrap, then page.keyboard.type). Read-only DOM inspection found the word displayed as a text node in div.code-line (inside div.code-layer > div.code-viewport > div.editor-wrap), all ordinary non-editable DIVs with isContentEditable=false. The only editable element inside the editing area is input.key-capture (aria-label 'Code input'), positioned off-screen at (-10000,-10000) with an empty value — it only receives keyboard events and does not show the source, which the criterion explicitly allows. No ready-made editor root markers (cm-editor, CodeMirror, monaco-editor, ace_editor, ProseMirror, tiptap, ql-editor, data-slate-editor, DraftEditor) appear on the editor element, its ancestors, or descendants. The source the user sees is drawn by ordinary non-editable elements, so the criterion passes.

criteria.name: cw_shared_saved_record
criteria.description: Create one new .js snippet with a unique title and a short unique source entered in the editor by typing or by pasting with the usual shortcut, and the Save control, and see any visible sign that the Save went through, such as a status message or the snippet appearing in the library; the response need not echo the saved fields. Then clear this origin's browser storage as described in the application notes and reload the page, so nothing held only in the browser survives. Find that snippet in the library, open it and confirm the exact title, filename and source. Reload once more and confirm them again. Fails if the snippet is missing after browser storage was cleared, if any of the three fields differs, or if the snippet disappears after the second reload. Leave the saved record in place.
criteria.reasoning: Created a new .js snippet: typed console.log("FROSTQUARTZ-7391"); into the editor with real key presses (verified the rendered editor text equaled the fixture), typed unique title 'Frostquartz 7391' and filename 'frostquartz7391.js', and clicked Save. Visible sign of success: status showed 'Saved · revision 1' and the snippet appeared in the Saved snippets library (count 0→1). Cleared this origin's browser storage (localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, Cache Storage, service workers, OPFS, cookies — verified empty) and reloaded. The snippet was still listed; clicking Open showed exact title 'Frostquartz 7391', filename 'frostquartz7391.js', and source console.log("FROSTQUARTZ-7391");. Reloaded a second time, clicked Open again, and confirmed all three fields identical. The snippet persisted across both reloads and was left in place.

criteria.name: cw_workspace_loads_and_reloads
criteria.description: Open / and wait for the page to load. The page must show the playground workspace with a code editing area, without a blank page or a fatal error. Reload the page: the workspace must load again. If the browser asks whether to leave the page, accept that dialog; a reload that waits for that dialog is not a failure. This checks only that the app is running and serves its workspace. Fails if the page is blank or shows only an error, if no code editing area is shown, or if the workspace does not load again after the reload. Do not type, press Run, save anything or judge any other feature here; other dimensions grade those.
criteria.reasoning: The playground loaded at http://localhost:3000/ with the full workspace: header ("Local Playground"), title and filename fields ("Untitled experiment" / "experiment.js"), a code editor region with a code input and line/column readout (Ln 1, Col 1) plus Undo/Redo/Format/Find/Replace controls, Run and Stop buttons, preview iframe, console, and a saved snippets library. No blank page or fatal error was shown. Reloading the page re-rendered the same workspace, again showing the "Code editor" region with its application element and code input; no leave-page dialog appeared and no error state was present. The app is running and serves its workspace on both the initial load and the reload.
